title: Module quiz: Scenario: structured data extraction

questions.stem: Scenario S6, structured data extraction, in which a pipeline validates every record and sends the doubtful ones to a person. Typed forms are right 38 times in 40 and handwritten forms 12 times in 20. The policy asks for 90 percent and at least 30 documents. What does the audit conclude?

options.text: Both kinds are ready, since the overall figure of the whole set is above the target
options.says: Ruled out because the average is not the test: "The overall figure plays no part in this decision".

options.text: Neither kind is ready, since the weaker kind drags the figure of the stronger one down
options.says: Ruled out because a kind is judged on its own documents: "A kind of document may go without a person only when two things hold".

options.text: The smaller kind is ready and the larger is not, since fewer forms mean fewer errors
options.says: Ruled out because a small sample is no evidence: "The minimum matters because ten correct documents are a small sample, and the target is a floor and not a ceiling."

options.text: The larger kind is ready and the smaller is not, since only the larger meets both conditions
options.says: Both conditions are checked per kind.

origin.section: What a kind of document needs before a person is removed

questions.stem: Scenario S6, structured data extraction, in which a pipeline validates every record and sends the doubtful ones to a person. A colleague asks why the audit counts an unchecked total only in documents accepted as valid. What is the answer?

options.text: A reviewed case was seen by someone, and a failed one never went out
options.says: Only an accepted record can carry an unchecked total.

options.text: Failed documents hold no total at all, so there would be nothing in them to count
options.says: Ruled out because the reason is who looked and not whether a total exists: "A document that went to a person was looked at, and a document that failed was never delivered".

options.text: Documents sent to a person are counted elsewhere, in the figure for wasted retries
options.says: Ruled out because the wasted-retry count is a different shape: "A wasted retry costs money and time and corrupts nothing, so it comes second."

options.text: The count would otherwise be larger than the number of documents that the run held
options.says: Ruled out because the counts are per shape and not capped by the run: "The audit counts an unchecked total only among documents accepted as valid."

questions.stem: Scenario S6, structured data extraction, in which a pipeline validates every record and sends the doubtful ones to a person. The example's by-kind line reads typed 2/2, scanned 1/2 and handwritten 0/2, under a policy of at least two documents and a target of 100 percent. Why is only the typed kind listed for automation?

options.text: It is the only kind that has a total printed in every one of its documents
options.says: Ruled out because totals are not the test: "A kind of document may go without a person only when two things hold".

options.text: It has a large enough sample and a high enough accuracy
options.says: The kind needs documents and accuracy.

options.text: It was the first kind to appear in the run, and the list stops after the first
options.says: Ruled out because the list is built per kind from evidence and not from order: "Only typed documents have earned automation."

options.text: It is the kind with the most documents behind it in the whole run
options.says: Ruled out because the test is a minimum and not the largest count, and each kind here has two documents: "the kind has at least a minimum number of documents behind it, and its accuracy is at least the target".

origin.section: What a kind of document needs before a person is removed

questions.stem: Scenario S6, structured data extraction, in which a pipeline validates every record and sends the doubtful ones to a person. A run shows a few invented vendor names and a long list of wasted retries. The team wants to begin with the retries, because they are far more frequent. What does the order of fixes say?

options.text: Begin with the retries, since frequency is the best guide to what a defect costs overall
options.says: Ruled out because frequency does not set it: "The order follows the damage a shape does downstream."

options.text: Fields come first, as a wrong entry that looks fine goes unseen downstream
Fix both at once, as the two shapes share one cause that sits in the schema
options.says: Ruled out because the audit names one fix first: "A run often shows several failure shapes at once, and the audit names one fix first."

options.text: Begin with the measurement, because both of the counts could be wrong in the first place
options.says: Ruled out because the measurement fault comes fourth: "An overstated figure is a measurement fault, fourth."
